quarterly_data.quarter: Teradyne press release: Teradyne Introduces Titan HP Platform with Burn-In (10-06-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Teradyne announced a production-ready system with enhanced burn-in capabilities on its Titan HP platform, aimed at high-power AI data center devices: instead of holding devices in banks of dedicated ovens, Titan HP holds each device at its target junction temperature while running a realistic device workload, with per-site thermal control and high per-device kilowatt power delivery, and an asynchronous slot architecture that loads and tests each slot independently. It can be used for system level test or reliability testing; test programs run on the Teradyne Atlas software platform. The release states Titan HP with enhanced burn-in 'is available today and deployed in production'. Jason Zee, VP and GM of the Integrated Systems Test division: 'Our customers are being asked to ship high-power AI silicon at reliability levels that used to belong to automotive.' The company says AI accelerators and cloud infrastructure devices are now entering the burn-in category, driven by the high cost of a single failed accelerator in a deployed rack, and that its per-device power roadmap extends to the levels future AI accelerators are expected to require. No customers named.
